To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GAA VNWFET is suitable for access device for future non-volatile memories such as resistive, phase change, and spin torque transfer random access memories.
the GAA vertical nanowire transistor has a potential to be used as an access element for various types of NVMs.

we have optimized the gate all around vertical transistor for the access element of future non volatile memories such as phase change random access, resistive random access and spin torque transfer random access memories.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of a vertical nanowire transistor for use as an access element for future NVM applications and the evaluation of the impact of the active device on its neighboring inactive devices in a cross bar memory array.
the design optimization of vertical nanowire field effect transistors (VNW-FET) for use in future nonvolatile memory applications.
the optimization of vertical nanowire transistor as access device in future non volatile memory devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimized GAA-VNWFET is a promising candidate to be used as the access element for future non-volatile memory devices.
GAA VNWFET can be a good choice for access device in future memory devices.
the optimized access transistor can be used in future NVM applications with the appropriate memory cell design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single device design can be used for all the memory devices and the device can be used in a range of current densities.
the GAA VNWFET can be used for future NVM applications as it has the ability to provide a wide range of ION and IOFF values, while maintaining a high ION/IOF ratio and low disturb.

the optimized access transistor can be used as a generic access device for future non volatile memories and can be used to achieve high performance in terms of ION/IOff and also to achieve high reliability in terms of read and write disturb.

the GAA vertical nanowire device is a very good candidate for access device of future NVMs.
by optimizing the access device we can achieve the desired read and write currents and reduce the read/write disturbance on neighboring cells in an array.
the GAA vertical nanowire transistor can be a viable candidate for future memory applications.
